117	/* Iterator helpers for the release-suppression check below: is this fret
118	 * needed again by an outstanding entry whose deadline falls at or before
119	 * `by_ms`? Bounding by the scheduled release time releases the fret between
120	 * separate notes (clean per-note command) and holds it only across genuinely
121	 * back-to-back notes, where releasing+repressing would just churn. */
122	static bool note_q_needs_by(uint8_t bit, uint32_t by_ms)
123	{
124	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < s_note_count; i++)
125	    {
126	        uint8_t idx = (uint8_t)((s_note_head + i) % TP_FIFO_CAP);
127	        const pending_note_t *n = &s_note_q[idx];
128	        if ((n->fret_mask & bit) && (int32_t)(n->assert_at_ms - by_ms) <= 0)
129	        {
130	            return true;
131	        }
132	    }
133	    return false;
134	}
135	
136	static bool strum_q_needs_by(uint8_t bit, uint32_t by_ms)
137	{
138	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < s_strum_count; i++)
139	    {
140	        uint8_t idx = (uint8_t)((s_strum_head + i) % TP_FIFO_CAP);
141	        const pending_strum_t *s = &s_strum_q[idx];
142	        if ((s->fret_mask & bit) && (int32_t)(s->strum_at_ms - by_ms) <= 0)
143	        {
144	            return true;
145	        }
146	    }
147	    return false;
148	}

160	/* Edge derivation:
161	 *   - presses_mask: rising edge of pressed
162	 *   - releases_mask: falling edge of pressed */
163	static void derive_edges(const detector_state_t *state,
164	                         uint8_t *presses_mask, uint8_t *releases_mask,
165	                         uint8_t *pressed_mask)
166	{
167	    uint8_t pm = 0u;
168	    uint8_t rm = 0u;
169	    uint8_t cm = 0u;
170	
171	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
172	    {
173	        bool pressed = state->fret[i].pressed != 0u;
174	        if (pressed) { cm |= s_fret_bit[i]; }
175	
176	        bool was_pressed = (s_prev_pressed_mask & s_fret_bit[i]) != 0u;
177	        if (pressed && !was_pressed) { pm |= s_fret_bit[i]; }
178	        if (!pressed && was_pressed) { rm |= s_fret_bit[i]; }
179	    }
180	
181	    s_prev_pressed_mask = cm;
182	    *presses_mask  = pm;
183	    *releases_mask = rm;
184	    *pressed_mask  = cm;
185	}
186	
187	static void chord_commit(void)
188	{
189	    if (note_q_full() || strum_q_full())
190	    {
191	        s_chord_open = false;
192	        s_chord_mask = 0u;
193	        return;
194	    }
195	
196	    uint32_t assert_at = s_now_ms + TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS - TP_FRET_EARLY_MS;
197	    uint32_t strum_at  = s_now_ms + TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS;
198	
199	    if (!strum_q_empty())
200	    {
201	        uint8_t  last_idx = (uint8_t)((s_strum_tail + TP_FIFO_CAP - 1u) % TP_FIFO_CAP);
202	        uint32_t earliest = s_strum_q[last_idx].strum_at_ms + TP_STRUM_PULSE_MS;
203	        if ((int32_t)(assert_at - earliest) < 0)
204	        {
205	            assert_at = earliest;
206	            strum_at  = assert_at + TP_FRET_EARLY_MS;
207	        }
208	    }
209	
210	    pending_note_t  n = { .assert_at_ms = assert_at, .fret_mask = s_chord_mask };
211	    pending_strum_t s = { .strum_at_ms  = strum_at,  .fret_mask = s_chord_mask };
212	    note_q_push(n);
213	    strum_q_push(s);
214	
215	    s_chord_open = false;
216	    s_chord_mask = 0u;
217	}
218	
219	static void process_notes(void)
220	{
221	    while (!note_q_empty())
222	    {
223	        const pending_note_t *n = &s_note_q[s_note_head];
224	        if ((int32_t)(s_now_ms - n->assert_at_ms) < 0) { break; }
225	
226	        for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
227	        {
228	            uint8_t bit = s_fret_bit[i];
229	            bool need = (n->fret_mask & bit) != 0u;
230	            bool have = (s_frets_active & bit) != 0u;
231	            if (need && !have)      { s_frets_active |= bit; }
232	            else if (!need && have) { s_frets_active &= (uint8_t)~bit; }
233	        }
234	        note_q_pop();
235	    }
236	}
237	
238	static void process_strums(void)
239	{
240	    while (!strum_q_empty())
241	    {
242	        const pending_strum_t *s = &s_strum_q[s_strum_head];
243	        if ((int32_t)(s_now_ms - s->strum_at_ms) < 0) { break; }
244	
245	        s_strum_active        = true;
246	        s_strum_direction     = !s_strum_direction;
247	        s_strum_release_at_ms = s_now_ms + TP_STRUM_PULSE_MS;
248	
249	        strum_q_pop();
250	    }
251	}
252	
253	static void process_releases(uint8_t live_pressed_mask)
254	{
255	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
256	    {
257	        uint8_t bit = s_fret_bit[i];
258	        if ((s_release_pending_mask & bit) == 0u) { continue; }
259	        if ((int32_t)(s_now_ms - s_release_at_ms[i]) < 0) { continue; }
260	        if (live_pressed_mask & bit) { continue; }
261	        /* Hold only if re-needed at/before this release (back-to-back); a need
262	         * further out releases now for a clean per-note command. */
263	        if (note_q_needs_by(bit, s_release_at_ms[i]) ||
264	            strum_q_needs_by(bit, s_release_at_ms[i])) { continue; }
265	
266	        s_frets_active        &= (uint8_t)~bit;
267	        s_release_pending_mask &= (uint8_t)~bit;
268	    }
269	}
270	
271	static void advance(uint8_t live_pressed_mask)
272	{
273	    if (s_chord_open && (int32_t)(s_now_ms - s_chord_start_ms) >= (int32_t)TP_CHORD_WINDOW_MS)
274	    {
275	        chord_commit();
276	    }
277	
278	    if (s_strum_active && (int32_t)(s_now_ms - s_strum_release_at_ms) >= 0)
279	    {
280	        s_strum_active = false;
281	    }
282	
283	    process_notes();
284	    process_strums();
285	    process_releases(live_pressed_mask);
286	
287	    uint8_t mask = s_frets_active;
288	    if (s_strum_active)
289	    {
290	        mask |= s_strum_direction ? TIMING_BIT_STRUM_UP : TIMING_BIT_STRUM_DOWN;
291	    }
292	    publish_mask(mask);
293	}

295	/* Build the per-frame TIMING snapshot from current pipeline state. Called
296	 * once per process_frame after advance() has settled all queues and the
297	 * publish_mask. Deadlines for empty queues are zeroed; host inspects the
298	 * count fields before treating *_at_ms as meaningful. */
299	static void fill_timing_snapshot(perf_timing_snapshot_t *snap)
300	{
301	    memset(snap, 0, sizeof(*snap));
302	    snap->now_ms = s_now_ms;
303	
304	    snap->chord_open   = s_chord_open ? 1u : 0u;
305	    snap->chord_mask   = s_chord_open ? s_chord_mask : 0u;
306	    snap->chord_age_ms = s_chord_open
307	                       ? (uint16_t)(s_now_ms - s_chord_start_ms)
308	                       : 0u;
309	
310	    snap->note_q_count = s_note_count;
311	    if (s_note_count > 0u)
312	    {
313	        const pending_note_t *head = &s_note_q[s_note_head];
314	        snap->note_head_mask  = head->fret_mask;
315	        snap->note_head_at_ms = head->assert_at_ms;
316	        uint8_t tail_union = 0u;
317	        for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < s_note_count; i++)
318	        {
319	            uint8_t idx = (uint8_t)((s_note_head + i) % TP_FIFO_CAP);
320	            tail_union |= s_note_q[idx].fret_mask;
321	        }
322	        snap->note_tail_mask = tail_union;
323	    }
324	
325	    snap->strum_q_count = s_strum_count;
326	    if (s_strum_count > 0u)
327	    {
328	        const pending_strum_t *head = &s_strum_q[s_strum_head];
329	        snap->strum_head_mask  = head->fret_mask;
330	        snap->strum_head_at_ms = head->strum_at_ms;
331	    }
332	    /* strum_dir toggles each fired strum; report the *next* direction
333	     * (what would fire if the front of strum_q reaches its deadline now). */
334	    snap->strum_dir_next = s_strum_direction ? 2u /*up*/ : 1u /*down*/;
335	
336	    snap->frets_active         = s_frets_active;
337	    snap->strum_active         = s_strum_active ? 1u : 0u;
338	    snap->release_pending_mask = s_release_pending_mask;
339	    snap->publish_mask         = s_output_mask;
340	    snap->strum_release_at_ms  = s_strum_active ? s_strum_release_at_ms : 0u;
341	
342	    if (s_release_pending_mask != 0u)
343	    {
344	        uint32_t min_at = 0xFFFFFFFFu;
345	        for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
346	        {
347	            if ((s_release_pending_mask & s_fret_bit[i]) == 0u) { continue; }
348	            if (s_release_at_ms[i] < min_at) { min_at = s_release_at_ms[i]; }
349	        }
350	        snap->release_min_at_ms = (min_at == 0xFFFFFFFFu) ? 0u : min_at;
351	    }
352	}

354	static void process_frame(const detector_state_t *state)
355	{
356	    /* Detector frame timestamps drive the clock so this is replay-
357	     * deterministic. timestamp_us is monotonic per spec §4.2.3. */
358	    s_now_ms = (uint32_t)(state->timestamp_us / 1000ull);
359	    s_last_frame_us = state->timestamp_us;
360	
361	    uint8_t presses, releases, pressed_mask;
362	    derive_edges(state, &presses, &releases, &pressed_mask);
363	
364	    if (presses)
365	    {
366	        if (!s_chord_open)
367	        {
368	            s_chord_open     = true;
369	            s_chord_start_ms = s_now_ms;
370	            s_chord_mask     = 0u;
371	        }
372	        s_chord_mask |= presses;
373	    }
374	
375	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
376	    {
377	        if (releases & s_fret_bit[i])
378	        {
379	            s_release_at_ms[i]      = s_now_ms + TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS;
380	            s_release_pending_mask |= s_fret_bit[i];
381	        }
382	    }
383	
384	    advance(pressed_mask);
385	
386	    PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_TP_TICK, state->frame_epoch,
387	                      (uint32_t)s_output_mask);
388	
389	    perf_timing_snapshot_t snap;
390	    fill_timing_snapshot(&snap);
391	    PerfLog_EmitTiming(state->frame_epoch, &snap);
392	}
393	
394	static void timing_pipeline_task(void *param)
395	{
396	    (void)param;
397	
398	    QueueHandle_t bus = Detector_BusQueue();
399	    configASSERT(bus != NULL);
400	
401	    LOG_INFO("TIMING: pipeline started\r\n");
402	
403	    for (;;)
404	    {
405	        detector_state_t state;
406	        if (xQueueReceive(bus, &state, pdMS_TO_TICKS(TP_TICK_MS)) == pdTRUE)
407	        {
408	            if ((detector_id_t)state.detector_id != Detector_GetActive())
409	            {
410	                continue;
411	            }
412	            process_frame(&state);
413	        }
414	        else
415	        {
416	            /* No new frame; advance the clock so deadlines that fell
417	             * between frames (strum pulses, release timers) still fire. */
418	            s_now_ms += TP_TICK_MS;
419	            advance(s_prev_pressed_mask);
420	        }
421	    }
422	}
423	
424	void TimingPipeline_Initialize(void)
425	{
426	    TaskHandle_t h = xTaskCreateStatic(timing_pipeline_task,
427	                                       "Timing",
428	                                       TP_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
429	                                       NULL,
430	                                       TP_TASK_PRIORITY,
431	                                       s_task_stack,
432	                                       &s_task_tcb);
433	    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_TIMING, h);
434	}
435	
436	void TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(bool enabled)
437	{
438	    if (enabled == s_pipeline_enabled)
439	    {
440	        return;
441	    }
442	    s_pipeline_enabled = enabled;
443	    if (!enabled)
444	    {
445	        /* Release the wire on disable so no frets stay held (the actuator's own
446	         * heartbeat would otherwise keep re-sending the last mask). */
447	        FretboardLink_Send(0u, (uint8_t)PERF_ACTUATOR_PRODUCER_TIMING);
448	    }
449	}
450	
451	bool TimingPipeline_IsEnabled(void)
452	{
453	    return s_pipeline_enabled;
454	}

17:3. Decide *what* to play and *when* (chord grouping, fret-early timing, strum scheduling).
18:4. Send the corresponding fret/strum commands to the actuator controller (the **fretboard** MCU).
21:7. **Observe game state from the screen** — recognize current menu / song-select / gameplay / pause / score-summary contexts via CV, expose high-level control verbs ("start single-player playthrough of song X", "advance menu", "exit to main menu") that translate into fret/strum command sequences sent through the same fretboard link.
27:- **Not the actuator.** Physical fret/strum GPIO drive lives on the fretboard MCU. marvin sends bitmask commands; fretboard converts them to button presses.

### 2.4 Latency budget (target, end-to-end)

| Stage | Budget | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| HDMI source → DDR (capture) | ≤ 16.7 ms | One frame @ 60 Hz; bounded by capture pipeline. |
| Detect on frame | ≤ 16.7 ms | One frame budget for CV; ADC path is separate and faster. |
| Timing pipeline → command emit | latency dominated by `STRUM_DELAY_MS` (≈ 200 ms) — intentional, not waste; compensates for sensor placement above strike line. |
| UART command → fretboard GPIO | ≤ 5 ms | Short fixed-format frame at ≥ 115 200 Bd. |
| Total user-visible latency | ≈ 200–250 ms | Tunable via `STRUM_DELAY_MS`, set per-game by calibration. |

The dominant fixed delay (`STRUM_DELAY_MS`) exists by design — the camera sees notes before they reach the strike line. Capture + detect + UART jitter is what we actually budget against.

## 4. Subsystems

### 4.1 Video capture & display ✅

Working end-to-end. See [`capture_pipeline.md`](capture_pipeline.md) and [`display_path.md`](display_path.md) for register-level detail. The video task (`video.c`, FreeRTOS) owns the capture pipeline and a frame queue that other tasks subscribe to. Display intent and capture intent are decoupled (commit `e28c497`); a software scaler can be inserted between capture and display when source ≠ panel native.

**What this subsystem owns:**
- TC358743 init, source detection, EDID, format negotiation.
- ISC DMA configuration and frame buffer rotation in DDR.
- XLCDC overlay window placement (pillarbox/letterbox) for the active source.
- Frame-ready notification to subscribers (CV detect, recording, UI overlay).

**What it doesn't own:**
- CV processing (§4.2).
- Recording / export (§4.6).
- UI widgets / chrome (§4.5) — only the pixel composition for the live-view layer.

### 4.2 CV detection pipeline + detector-state bus 🚧

#### 4.2.1 Role

This is what makes marvin the *reference detector*. It runs computer-vision note detection on captured frames and publishes a structured detector-state record per frame onto a shared bus. Other detectors (fretboard ADC; future Edge-AI unit) publish onto the same bus. The timing pipeline (§4.4) consumes the bus.

#### 4.2.2 Detector model

A **detector** is anything that turns observation data into a `detector_state_t` event. marvin will host at least:

- `cv_marvin_v1` — the reference vision detector. Reads RGB888-packed (3 B/pixel) frames from the video frame queue; emits one `detector_state_t` per frame.
- `adc_fretboard` — runs on top of raw ADC samples streamed from the fretboard MCU (§4.3); emits `detector_state_t` events at the fretboard's 240 Hz rate.

Future detectors may include alternate CV algorithms running in parallel for comparison, or off-board detectors (Edge-AI MCU) feeding state in over UART/Ethernet.

#### 4.2.3 detector_state record (canonical shape)

```
typedef struct {
    uint32_t frame_epoch;     // master sync token (§4.6.4)
    uint64_t timestamp_us;    // monotonic, marvin-local
    uint8_t  detector_id;     // 0=cv_marvin_v1, 1=adc_fretboard, ...
    uint8_t  reserved[3];
    struct {
        uint8_t  pressed;     // 0/1 hard call
        uint16_t confidence;  // 0..65535, detector-defined
        uint16_t raw_value;   // detector-defined: ADC sample, pixel mean, etc.
    } fret[5];                // FRET_GREEN..FRET_ORANGE
} detector_state_t;
```

Fields are fixed-width, naturally aligned, little-endian — this is also the on-disk record layout for the state log (§4.6.5). `frame_epoch` is the master clock for cross-detector and cross-recording sync.

#### 4.2.4 Bus mechanics

- A single FreeRTOS queue (`xDetectorStateQueue`) carries `detector_state_t` records, one entry per detector emit.
- The timing pipeline task (§4.4) is the sole consumer.
- The recording task (§4.6) snoops the queue via a side-channel: each producer publishes simultaneously to the timing-pipeline queue and to a recording stream buffer. (Single producer→multiple consumers is implemented by tee'ing inside each detector, not by a broker; keeps queue semantics blocking and simple.)
- Detectors run on their own FreeRTOS tasks (one per detector instance) so a slow detector cannot stall the frame pipeline.

#### 4.2.5 Reference-detector responsibilities

`cv_marvin_v1` is a *first-class* subsystem, not a debug aid. Its detector state is the ground-truth label for any reference-data recording (§4.6). Implications:

- Algorithm changes are versioned (`cv_marvin_v1`, `cv_marvin_v2`, …). The version is stamped into recordings so training data stays attributable.
- Calibration (sensor/strike-line ROIs in pixel space) is stored in the system config (§4.7) and reproducibly applied at startup.
- The detector must run within one frame-time (≤ 16.7 ms) on Cortex-A5 — concrete algorithm choice is a future decision, but the budget is set.

#### 4.2.6 Open questions surfaced here

- Initial CV algorithm — pixel-mean threshold per ROI, edge-trough, optical-flow-based, or learned. (Defer; bring up the simplest first to validate end-to-end.)
- ADC-detector logic location — port `fretboard/fret_button.c`'s detection (hysteresis edges) into marvin (`adc_fretboard` runs on raw samples), or have fretboard pre-process and stream edges. (Default: marvin runs the detector on raw samples; fretboard stays dumb.)

### 4.3 Fretboard link ✅

**Transport.** The shipping default is the **10BASE-T1S bus** (`user.cmake` hard-sets `MARVIN_FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT=T1S`; see [`docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](../../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md)): marvin is the PLCA coordinator and the guitar/fretboard nodes are followers. The **FLEXCOM1 USART** below is the fallback transport, selected by building with `MARVIN_FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT=UART`. The 1-byte command and 17-byte ADC frame formats are identical on either transport. In the T1S build FLEXCOM1 is free and instead hosts the **fauxmote link** (see below and §4.9).

Direct **FLEXCOM1 USART** link between marvin and the fretboard MCU — a plain UART wire, no USB. marvin's `PA28` (FLEXCOM1_IO0, `GUITAR_TX`) and `PA29` (FLEXCOM1_IO1, `GUITAR_RX`) connect to the fretboard's SERCOM1 (`PB01` RX / `PB00` TX). Both ends run **500 000 baud, 8N1**. The FLEXCOM1 USART runs in Harmony ring-buffer mode so RX never drops bytes between reads. (Was FLEXCOM2 until the console moved onto FLEXCOM2 — see §4.9.)

- **Marvin → fretboard:** command bitmask (which frets to assert + strum direction). 1-byte bitmask, no framing. `fretboard_link_task` writes the latest mask via `FLEXCOM1_USART_Write`.
- **Fretboard → marvin:** raw ADC stream (5 channels × 16-bit) at 240 Hz, in a 17-byte start/end-bracketed frame (`0x03 … 0xFC`, with `sample_seq` + `applied_mask`). The FLEXCOM1 RX ring fills continuously from its ISR; a persistent read-threshold notification wakes `fretboard_rx_task`, which drains the ring, resyncs on the frame markers, and republishes each valid frame as a `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` perf-log record (default-disabled, host enables via `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK`). This is the on-board capture path until the SD-card recorder lands; it's also the substrate for the future `adc_fretboard` detector (§4.2).
- **Standalone fallback:** when marvin's timing pipeline is disabled (see §4.4 and §6), the fretboard runs its own existing chord FIFO (`fret_button.c`) and continues to stream ADC + emitted-command telemetry to marvin for capture/display.
- **Fauxmote link (T1S build only):** with the guitar node on T1S, FLEXCOM1 is free, so in the T1S build marvin brings up a link to the fauxmote board (ESP32 Wiimote emulator, §7 top-level SPEC) on FLEXCOM1 (`net/fauxmote/fauxmote_link.c`, `Fauxmote_Initialize`). It mirrors every gameplay bitmask — `FretboardLink_Send` taps `Fauxmote_SendGuitarMask` — and is inspected/controlled via the `fauxmote` console command (§4.9).

### 4.4 Timing pipeline 🚧

Centralized on marvin by default. Owns:

- Chord-accumulation window (`CHORD_WINDOW_MS` ≈ 20–40 ms).
- Pending-chord FIFO with per-chord `press_at` / `strum_at` ticks.
- Per-fret release scheduling.
- Strum direction alternation and pulse generation.
- `STRUM_DELAY_MS` / `FRET_EARLY_MS` / `STRUM_PULSE_MS` constants — initial values port from `tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md` and `firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md`.

**Disable / handoff mode:** an operator-mode toggle (§6) deactivates marvin's pipeline. fretboard then runs its own existing pipeline; marvin still ingests ADC + emitted-command telemetry for recording/display, but does not emit commands.

### 4.5 UI / operator surface 🚧

10.1″ 1280×800 LVDS panel + maxtouch capacitive touch. Functional surfaces required:

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-15 14:54:36Z)**_

Confirmed the full picture. The guitar node ([t1s_follower.c:282](firmware/guitar/config.mcc/src/t1s_follower.c#L282)) does `buttons_apply_mask` the instant a T1S frame lands — zero timing knowledge. All timing lives in [timing_pipeline.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/timing_pipeline.c) on marvin, and the wire protocol is "assert this mask *now*."

You're right that there's a muddle. But I think it's worth being precise about *which* timing is misplaced, because there are actually three different clocks fused into one `STRUM_DELAY_MS`, and only some of them are the actuator's business.

## Three timing concepts, currently all in the pipeline

**1. Observation lead** — `STRUM_DELAY_MS` (400ms). The camera ROI sits *above* the strike line, so a note is detected ~400ms before it should be played. The spec comment even says so: *"compensates for sensor placement above strike line."* This is a **detector/geometry** property — it's about where the ROI is and how fast the highway scrolls. It is *not* a scheduling choice and *definitely* not an actuator property. It's masquerading as a pipeline constant.

**2. Musical scheduling** — `CHORD_WINDOW_MS`, `FRET_EARLY_MS`, `STRUM_PULSE_MS`, release scheduling, strum-direction alternation, the back-to-back hold logic. This is the "decide what to play and when" layer. It genuinely belongs in the pipeline/scheduler. This is correct where it is.

**3. Mechanical actuation advance** — solenoid rise time, GPIO propagation. *Does not exist today* (open-drain GPIO is effectively instant, so advance = 0). When solenoids arrive, whoever drives them must fire ~5–20ms **early**. This is an **actuator** property, and it varies per actuator rig — marvin may drive the GPIO guitar node today and a solenoid rig tomorrow, each with a different (and possibly per-fret, or fret-vs-strum-different) advance.

The bug in the current shape isn't that timing #2 is in the pipeline — it should be. It's that #1 is mislabeled as a scheduler constant, and #3 has nowhere to live except by being smeared into `STRUM_DELAY_MS`, which couples marvin to a specific actuator's mechanics.

## The crux: how does the actuator get "press at time T"?

Your framing — command = "press this button at this time," actuator subtracts its own advance — requires the *when* to travel over the wire. Today the wire carries only *what* ("assert now"). There are two ways to close that gap:

**Option A — Dumb wire stays; marvin applies the actuator's declared advance.**
The actuator's mechanical advance is a *property owned by the actuator node* (a capability/config value: `guitar` reports advance=0, a solenoid rig reports advance=15ms, maybe per-bit). marvin *knows* that value (static config or a T1S capability exchange) and subtracts it when it decides the "now" moment to emit the bare mask. Wire protocol unchanged, no shared clock, no node buffering.
- ✅ Minimal; fits static-allocation, single-emit-point today.
- ✅ Correctly *locates the knowledge* with the actuator (config declared by the node), just applies it centrally.
- ⚠️ Link jitter is in the timing path (fine on lightly-loaded PLCA — sub-ms).
- ⚠️ Per-fret / fret-vs-strum advance gets awkward if it's rich.

**Option B — Timestamped commands; node applies its own advance (your instinct).**
Wire protocol becomes `(mask, strike_time_T)` in a shared time base. Node buffers and fires each command at `T − advance` off its local clock. marvin's scheduler works purely in strike-line time and never holds a command to its deadline — it emits early.
- ✅ Cleanest separation; node owns *and applies* its mechanics; scheduler is pure.
- ✅ Removes link jitter from the trigger; node can run tight local sequences (seat frets → then strum).
- ❌ Needs a shared clock/epoch across T1S nodes, command buffering + a scheduler on the node, and a protocol change (1-byte mask → timestamped frame). Real infrastructure.

**My recommendation:** do the *conceptual* re-layering now regardless of A/B, because that's the part that's actually wrong today, and it's cheap:

1. **Move `STRUM_DELAY_MS` out of "scheduling" and name it what it is** — a detector/observation-lead calibration. Cleanest: have the detector stamp a strike-line-referenced time per pressed edge (`strike_at = timestamp_us + observation_lead`), so the pipeline schedules purely in strike-line time and has no `STRUM_DELAY` of its own. That also makes per-detector leads possible (CV ROI vs ADC have different leads).
2. **Introduce an explicit `actuator_advance` concept even while it's 0**, owned by the actuator node as declared config, and go with **Option A** — marvin applies it. It's the minimal thing that puts the knowledge in the right place and unblocks solenoids without building a distributed clock you don't need yet.
3. Keep **Option B in your back pocket**: adopt it only if/when link jitter or on-node multi-solenoid sequencing actually demands local scheduling. The Option-A config value (`actuator_advance`) becomes the exact number the node would apply in Option B, so nothing is wasted.

Net: pipeline keeps timing #2 (scheduling), detector owns #1 (observation lead), actuator owns #3 (mechanical advance) — applied by marvin for now, movable to the node later.

This is a §4.4/§4.2 architectural decision and it interacts with open **Q11** (command-path arbitration). Rather than restate it in chat, per the repo's journal-first rule I'd like to write this three-layer model + the A/B decision into `firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md` (and probably a one-line note in spec §4.4 that `STRUM_DELAY` is observation-lead, not actuation delay).

Two things I want your call on before I record anything:

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-15 15:02:08Z)**_

Great questions and choices. Let me answer the T1S timing part directly, then record this.

**Is there timing built into T1S?** Not a clock, no. Worth separating two things:

- **PLCA (the 802.3cg reconciliation sublayer)** gives you *determinism* — bounded, low media-access latency and jitter via round-robin transmit opportunities by node ID. That's a latency guarantee, **not** a shared time base. It does not distribute a clock or timestamps.
- **Actual time sync** over Ethernet is IEEE 1588 / 802.1AS (PTP/gPTP), which needs hardware timestamping. Interestingly, your TC6 stack *does* surface a receive timestamp — that `uint64_t *rxTimestamp` in the RX callback at [t1s_follower.c:412](firmware/guitar/config.mcc/src/t1s_follower.c#L412) comes from the LAN8651 MACPHY. So HW RX timestamps exist if you ever wanted tight sync.

But for Option B you almost certainly **don't** want full PTP. The precision budget is coarse — solenoid advance is ~5–20ms and you need maybe ±2–5ms — and PLCA already bounds the jitter. So the pragmatic path is exactly what you guessed: **marvin periodically broadcasts a sync frame carrying its `frame_epoch`/timestamp; each follower disciplines a free-running local timer to it.** That's a few ms of accuracy for almost no infrastructure, versus a full PTP servo. I'll record that as the recommended sync mechanism *if* B is ever adopted, with "LAN8651 HW timestamps are available for tighter sync" as the escape hatch.

Now let me capture the model and decisions in the journal. Let me find the right sections.

204	| 2026-07-01 | **UI: paint every screen canvas once at boot; show/hide is repaint-free. Fixes the ~0.5–1 s first-touch lag after opening/closing the nav drawer or song-select modal.** Root cause: Legato defers all touch input while its renderer is non-idle (`handleTouchDown`/up/move return `LE_EVENT_DEFERRED` when `leIsDrawing()`, `legato_input.c`), re-queuing the event every 10 ms `LEGATO_Tasks` tick. 306	- **QSPI NOR (`SST26VF064BA`, 8 MB) storage tiering — driver bring-up DONE on hardware (2026-06-28), settings approach settled, splash + assets open.** QSPI PLIB + `DRV_SST26` (SQI) bring-up is **confirmed on hardware** via the `qspi` console smoke test (session log 2026-06-28): JEDEC `BF 26 43`, geometry 8 MiB (read 1×8388608, write page 256×32768, erase 4096×2048), and erase/page-program/read-back all verify clean. So these are now **answered**: the driver's `ResetFlash→EnableQuadIO→UnlockFlash` handles the global block-protection unlock automatically (erase/write work with no manual `ULBPR`), and `DRV_SST26_Tasks` pumping is a non-issue (no poll timeout). Settings → QSPI EEPROM-emulation is decided, and **read throughput is now characterized and integrity-verified** (2026-06-28 decision log + session log): GCLK=200 MHz → 100 MHz QSCK, **XDMAC mem2mem = 18.2 MB/s → ~225 ms for a 4 MB splash, ~3× faster than SD**; `qspi verify` clean at 1 MiB × 4 passes on both driver and XDMAC paths. So splash-on-QSPI is **viable and decided GO** via XDMAC ch1 mem2mem (cacheable-MMU and CRM ruled out; RX-triggered streaming → ~80 ms deferred as a mini-project). **Partition map is locked** (`flash/qspi_layout.h`, decision log 2026-06-28): splash `0x000000` (4 MiB) · assets `0x400000` (~3.98 MiB) · settings `0x7FC000` (16 KiB). **Both runtime consumers are built + confirmed on hardware (2026-06-28):** (1) the **settings ring-log** (`flash/settings.c`, EEPROM-emulation; backlight persists across power-cycle); (2) the **splash read** (`splash.c` reads `QSPI_SPLASH_OFFSET` via `DRV_SST26_Read` — **263 ms, splash shows with the SD card removed**). Host→QSPI **provisioning** is via u-boot `sf` over JTAG (`openocd/program-qspi.*` + `qspi_console.py`) — no SD card-swapping for assets. The splash read uses `DRV_SST26_Read` not XDMAC: at 263 ms it's already ~as fast as XDMAC (~225 ms), so XDMAC-for-splash isn't worth the ~40 ms. **Still open:** the **assets read-side** consumer (icons/fonts/album-art templates from `QSPI_ASSETS_OFFSET`) is unbuilt — the provisioning tool already writes that region. **at91bootstrap lives on NAND and does not touch the QSPI — we own the full 8 MB at the app level (QSPI splash is firmware-only, no bootstrap change).** NAND (`MX30LF4G28AD`, 512 MB) holds the app image (at91bootstrap copies it to DDR at boot); SD card stays for recordings/keyframes/results/bulk art. **Note:** the 200 MHz GCLK is an MCC clock-config change — verify it survives/needs-reapply on MCC regen, and re-run `qspi verify` after any QSPI MCC regen.

308	  **Load-time estimate vs. SD (measured 2026-06-28):** SD does the 4 MB raw RGBA8888 splash (1280×800×4 = 4.1 MB) in **~300 ms bringup + ~450 ms read** (~9 MB/s effective). QSPI eliminates the bringup (~1–5 ms) and reads faster: SST26 in SQI quad gives ~45 MB/s at the 104 MHz part max (~90 ms), down to ~25 MB/s if the controller caps SCK near 50 MHz (~165 ms) — so **~90–165 ms read vs. SD's 450 ms (~3–5× on the read alone), ~95–170 ms total vs. ~750 ms (~4–7× end-to-end)**. Assumes DMA from the memory-mapped region (a CPU `memcpy` is slower per-access). Endgame for a static splash: if the LCDC can scan straight out of memory-mapped QSPI (XIP), the DDR copy is skipped and load time → ~0 (at the cost of holding the QSPI bus during scanout). RGB565 (2 MB) halves the read numbers. Confirm the actual SCK rate on hardware before trusting these.

Patch **both** hooks to emit a marker (even a raw fixed-string DBGU write — heap is full / stack is corrupt, so avoid large stack frames and dynamic work) before the spin; this is an MCC re-apply patch (freertos_hooks.c is generated). marvin: actuator-advance seam (timing re-layer P1)

Separate the actuator's mechanical latency from the pipeline's scheduling
clock so "press this button at this time" and "fire early enough for the
solenoid to seat" are owned by the right layers.

- fretboard_link.h: FRETBOARD_ACTUATOR_ADVANCE_MS declares the active
  actuator node's mechanical advance (open-drain guitar node = 0; a future
  solenoid rig sets its rise time). An actuator-layer property.

  strum fire, fret release) fire_now = now + advance ms early. Chord window
  and strum-pulse release stay on the real clock (aggregation / emit-anchored
  pulse width). Wire byte stays a bare "assert now" mask (Option A).

Behavior-preserving at advance = 0 (current guitar node). Also drops
TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS 400 -> 250 (observation-lead tuning). Model + phased plan
in firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md (2026-07-15).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

158	static float brightness(const float bgr[3])
159	{
160	    float m = bgr[0];
161	    if (bgr[1] > m) { m = bgr[1]; }
162	    if (bgr[2] > m) { m = bgr[2]; }
163	    return m;

166	/* Color-filtered signal scaled by (max-min)/max so white/gray patches
167	 * produce near-zero signal regardless of camera white balance. */
168	static float color_signal(const float bgr[3], const color_filter_t *f)
169	{
170	    float cmax = brightness(bgr);
171	    if (cmax < 1.0f) { return 0.0f; }
172	    float cmin = bgr[0];
173	    if (bgr[1] < cmin) { cmin = bgr[1]; }
174	    if (bgr[2] < cmin) { cmin = bgr[2]; }
175	    float sat = (cmax - cmin) / cmax;
176	
177	    float target = f->target[0]*bgr[0] + f->target[1]*bgr[1] + f->target[2]*bgr[2];
178	    float reject = f->reject[0]*bgr[0] + f->reject[1]*bgr[1] + f->reject[2]*bgr[2];
179	    if (reject < 0.0f) { reject = 0.0f; }
180	    return (target - reject) * sat;
181	}

196	    uint16_t       fw   = frame->width;

199	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)

204	        sample_patch_bgr(fbuf, fw, fh, s.ex, s.ey, edge_bgr);
205	
206	        float hd = brightness(hold_bgr);

212	        else if (s_pressed[i] && hd < hold_release) { s_pressed[i] = false; }
213

225	        state.fret[i].confidence = (uint16_t)c;
226

/* PERF_REC_DETECTOR_CONFIG — cv_marvin_v1 per-fret configuration. Static
 * today (compile-time tables); becomes runtime-tunable when M6 calibration
 * UI lands. Emitted on connect-up edge and on change so the host always
 * has a current copy. Sample coords are in capture-frame space (matching
 * STRIP record (x, y) anchors). Floats are IEEE 754 little-endian — same
 * representation on both sides. Used by the host to render sample
 * dots / threshold reference lines onto STRIP canvases. */
typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
{
    perf_hdr_t hdr;
    uint16_t   sensor_hx[FRET_COUNT];          /* hold-sensor x per fret */
    uint16_t   sensor_hy[FRET_COUNT];          /* hold-sensor y per fret */
    uint16_t   sensor_ex[FRET_COUNT];          /* edge-sensor x per fret */
    uint16_t   sensor_ey[FRET_COUNT];          /* edge-sensor y per fret */
    float      hold_thresh;                    /* CV_HOLD_THRESH (brightness) */
    float      hold_release_frac;              /* CV_HOLD_RELEASE_FRAC */
    float      edge_thresh;                    /* CV_EDGE_THRESH */
    float      color_target_b[FRET_COUNT];     /* per-fret target weights */
    float      color_target_g[FRET_COUNT];
    float      color_target_r[FRET_COUNT];
    float      color_reject_b[FRET_COUNT];     /* per-fret reject weights */
    float      color_reject_g[FRET_COUNT];
    float      color_reject_r[FRET_COUNT];
} perf_rec_detector_config_t;

/* PERF_REC_ACTUATOR — emitted on every FretboardLink_Send call (i.e. on
 * intent), one record per call. Closes the gap between TIMING.publish_mask
 * (intent on the timing pipeline side) and FBL_SEND STAMP (a byte hit the
 * USB DMA): with multiple producers (timing_pipeline, manual_control, future
 * game_state_controller per spec §4.8), the wire byte alone doesn't say
 * who asserted what.
 *
 * intended_mask: what the producer asked for this Send (low 7 bits).
 * asserted_mask: what's currently held on the link (last byte queued).
 * strum_dir: from the bit pattern (0=none, 1=down, 2=up).
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-15 15:35:01Z)**_

Confirmed the layout, and it's telling: the command **producers** are already scattered — `timing_pipeline` and `manual_control` in `actuator/`, but `game_controller` in `game/`. And the pipeline pulls from the bus with a timeout ([timing_pipeline.c:420](firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/timing_pipeline.c#L420)). That informs both answers.

## Q1 — does the timing pipeline belong in `actuator/`?

Conceptually, no. After P1/P2 we made the three layers explicit, and the pipeline is the **middle "decide" layer** — a peer of detector and actuator, which is exactly how spec §4.4 frames it (peer of §4.2 detector, §4.3 link). `actuator/` today is really "command producers + the link sink," and that grouping is already inconsistent (game_controller, also a producer, lives in `game/`).

The clean structure that matches the model:
- `detector/` — sensing (owns observation lead)
- a new `scheduler/` (or `timing/`) — the pipeline: the detector→command decision layer
- `actuator/` — the **sink**: `fretboard_link` (transport) + the mechanical advance; producers live where their logic lives (`manual_control` is arguably a UI/operator concern, `game_controller` already in `game/`).

A sharper observation: post-re-layering, "timing" is now distributed across *all three* layers (lead → detector, scheduling → pipeline, advance → actuator). So `timing_pipeline` under `actuator/` is doubly loose — the pipeline's actual unique job is **command scheduling/arbitration**, not "timing" broadly. If we move it, `scheduler/` describes it better than `timing/`.

**Recommendation:** extract it to its own dir *if* we want the source tree to encode the architecture (I think it's worth it — the inconsistency with `game_controller` shows the current grouping isn't a real rule). Cost is mechanical churn: `user.cmake` source list, include paths, git history/blame. Low risk, no behavior change. If you'd rather not churn now, the layering is still correct in code — it's only the folder name that's loose.

## Q2 — should the pipeline pull from the detector, or should the detector push into it?

**Keep pull.** And note it's already the right shape: detectors *push onto a queue* (the bus), the pipeline *pulls off it* — a decoupled queue, not a direct call. That's correct for three concrete reasons:

1. **The pipeline is a time-driven state machine, not purely event-driven.** It has deadlines that fire *between* detector frames (strum-pulse release, fret release). The pull-with-timeout loop (`xQueueReceive(..., TP_TICK_MS)`) unifies "new frame arrived" and "time passed, advance deadlines" into one clock. A push model would still need a separate timer for the between-frame advance — splitting the pipeline's clock across two mechanisms. This is the strongest argument.
2. **Active-detector arbitration is a consumer-side policy.** The pipeline reads `Detector_GetActive()` and ignores other sources. With push, either every detector checks "am I active?" before calling (scatters policy), or you add a broker.
3. **The bus already fans out.** The recording tee and multiple detectors publish to the same queue; a shared push-to-bus / pull-from-bus supports that. Direct detector→pipeline calls would over-couple them.

So: don't switch to detector-calls-pipeline. If anything, the current model is *more* than pull — it's a proper bus, which is right.

The one subtlety worth naming: between frames the pipeline *extrapolates* its clock (`s_now_ms += TP_TICK_MS`) rather than reading a real monotonic source, so it assumes the tick period is accurate. That's fine today, but if jitter ever matters, driving the tick-advance off a real timer read (not a fixed increment) is the refinement — orthogonal to pull-vs-push.

---

Net: **Q2 is already right — leave it.** **Q1 is genuinely a bit off** — the pipeline is the scheduler layer, misfiled under `actuator/`.

Want me to extract the pipeline into its own `scheduler/` dir (and record the rationale in the journal), just record the decision without moving files yet, or leave it and move on?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-15 15:43:42Z)**_

Both are good calls. Let me reason through each.

## Q1 — should the scheduler live in `game/`?

Yes — I think `game/` is a better home than a standalone `scheduler/`, and here's why it's actually the *right* answer rather than just convenient:

The timing pipeline and `game_controller` are **two halves of the same job — autonomously operating Guitar Hero.** `game_controller` drives the menus/session setup; the timing pipeline plays the note highway. Spec **Q11** is precisely about arbitrating between them because *they're mutually exclusive* (menu vs. gameplay). Two mutually-exclusive command producers that need explicit arbitration are siblings — putting them in the same module makes that arbitration local and obvious instead of spanning `game/` ↔ `actuator/`.

So the clean split becomes:
- `detector/` — sensing
- `game/` — the game-domain brain: observe (`gameplay_engine`) + decide (`game_controller` for menus, `timing_pipeline` for notes)
- `actuator/` — pure command **sink**: `fretboard_link` (transport) + mechanical advance

The "reusable generic scheduler" counter-argument is YAGNI — the pipeline is built for GH3 and coordinated with `game_controller`, same as the detector is GH3-specific in practice. 

One leftover: **`manual_control` is *not* game logic** — it's operator override. It shouldn't follow the pipeline into `game/`; it belongs in `actuator/` (or `ui/`). So the move is just `timing_pipeline` → `game/`, leaving `actuator/` = link + advance + manual_control-if-we-leave-it.

## Q2 — arbitration moves to the detector module (bus carries only the active detector)

Agreed, and it's clean **because the detector bus is already pipeline-only.** I confirmed `Detector_BusQueue()` is consumed by exactly one task — the pipeline ([timing_pipeline.c:412](firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/timing_pipeline.c#L412)). Recording and the UI feed use *separate* paths (`PerfLog_EmitDetector` → perf-log queue; `dashboard_feed` → its own queue). So gating the bus to the active detector doesn't cost the recorder its side-by-side data — that never flowed through this queue.

Concretely: add a single choke point in the detector module —

```c
void Detector_Publish(const detector_state_t *s) {
    if ((detector_id_t)s->detector_id == s_active) {
        (void)xQueueSend(s_bus_queue, s, 0);
    }
}
```

Detectors call `Detector_Publish(&state)` instead of raw `xQueueSend`; the pipeline drops its `if (detector_id != Detector_GetActive()) continue;` filter and trusts the bus. Arbitration lives in one place (detector module), the pipeline gets simpler, and the bus's meaning becomes "the active detector's stream."

Two small notes:
- **Enable ≠ active.** Recording wants *enabled* detectors emitting their perf/UI records (`PerfLog_EmitDetector` stays unconditional in `detect_frame`); only the *bus push* is gated on active. So a non-active detector still runs and still feeds training data — it just doesn't reach the pipeline.
- **Stale-on-switch:** when active changes, a couple of old-source records may already sit in the shallow bus queue; the pipeline would consume them for ~1–2 frames. Harmless, but if we want it crisp we can drain the bus on switch inside `Detector_SetActive`.

---

Both are low-risk and no behavior change (Q2 is behavior-identical since the pipeline already filtered to the active detector; Q1 is a pure move). Q1 is the churny one (`user.cmake` source list, include paths, git blame).

Proven by the detector-fb probe: clean per-note labels took overfit frets 0.94→0.99 (edge-ai journal 2026-06-03). Releasing per-note makes the command a function of the observable. Physical legato (avoiding release/repress churn on fast Expert runs) moves to a future fretboard *lazy actuator* layer; until then marvin's own play release-represses, which is fine at hard-mode note spacing. 257	#### 4.2.4 Bus mechanics
258	
259	- A single FreeRTOS queue (`xDetectorStateQueue`) carries `detector_state_t` records, one entry per detector emit.
260	- The timing pipeline task (§4.4) is the sole consumer.
261	- The recording task (§4.6) snoops the queue via a side-channel: each producer publishes simultaneously to the timing-pipeline queue and to a recording stream buffer. (Single producer→multiple consumers is implemented by tee'ing inside each detector, not by a broker; keeps queue semantics blocking and simple.)
262	- Detectors run on their own FreeRTOS tasks (one per detector instance) so a slow detector cannot stall the frame pipeline.

288	### 4.4 Timing pipeline 🚧
289	
290	Centralized on marvin by default. Schedules **in the strike-line time base** — it acts on each detector record's `strike_at_ms` (§4.2.3) rather than holding an observation-delay constant of its own; the observation lead now lives with the detector. Owns:
291	
292	- Chord-accumulation window (`CHORD_WINDOW_MS` ≈ 20–40 ms).
293	- Pending-chord FIFO with per-chord `press_at` / `strum_at` ticks (both derived from `strike_at_ms`).
294	- Per-fret release scheduling.
295	- Strum direction alternation and pulse generation.
296	- `FRET_EARLY_MS` / `STRUM_PULSE_MS` musical-scheduling constants — initial values port from `tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md` and `firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md`. (The former `STRUM_DELAY_MS` is now the detector's per-config `observation_lead_ms`.)
297	- **Actuator advance:** subtracts the active actuator node's declared mechanical advance (`FRETBOARD_ACTUATOR_ADVANCE_MS`, 0 for the open-drain guitar node) when deciding when to emit, so a solenoid rig's rise time lands the effect on the strike line. The wire byte stays a bare "assert now" mask (Option A; see journal 2026-07-15).
298	
299	**Disable / handoff mode:** an operator-mode toggle (§6) deactivates marvin's pipeline. fretboard then runs its own existing pipeline; marvin still ingests ADC + emitted-command telemetry for recording/display, but does not emit commands.

it (dropped raw xQueueSend + bus plumbing); timing_pipeline dropped its
active-detector filter. Bus now carries a single source's stream; behavior
identical. Recording still captures all enabled detectors via the separate
PerfLog path.

Spec §4.2.4/§4.4 and journal updated. Follow-up noted: TIMING_BIT_* wire-mask
defines should move from the scheduler header to the actuator/wire layer.

#ifndef GUITAR_CMD_H
#define GUITAR_CMD_H

/* Guitar controller command bitmask — the wire format marvin sends to the
 * actuator node over the fretboard link (§4.3). Shared vocabulary for every
 * producer that builds a mask (timing pipeline, manual control, game
 * controller) and everything that interprets one (the link, the UI). Mirrors
 * the receiver's layout: firmware/fretboard cmd_receive.h and the guitar
 * node's T1S command bits.
 *
 *   bit 0 = green   bit 1 = red    bit 2 = yellow
 *   bit 3 = blue    bit 4 = orange bit 5 = strum-down bit 6 = strum-up */

#define GUITAR_BTN_GREEN       (1u << 0)
#define GUITAR_BTN_RED         (1u << 1)
#define GUITAR_BTN_YELLOW      (1u << 2)
#define GUITAR_BTN_BLUE        (1u << 3)
#define GUITAR_BTN_ORANGE      (1u << 4)
#define GUITAR_BTN_STRUM_DOWN  (1u << 5)
#define GUITAR_BTN_STRUM_UP    (1u << 6)
#define GUITAR_BTN_FRET_MASK   0x1Fu   /* the five fret bits */
#define GUITAR_BTN_VALID_MASK  0x7Fu   /* all valid command bits */

#endif

```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-15 18:25:05Z)**_

Confirmed a couple of real things. Here's what's genuinely worth looking at, most-substantive first:

## Substantive

**1. CV strike time is anchored to *detect* time, not *capture* time.** `cv_marvin_v1` stamps `timestamp_us = xTaskGetTickCount()` at the moment the CV task *processes* the frame ([cv_marvin_v1.c:193](firmware/marvin/default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c#L193)), and `Video_FrameInfo` carries only `frame_count` — no capture timestamp. So the capture→detect latency (frame sits in the queue + CV task scheduling) folds into `strike_at_ms`. `observation_lead_ms` absorbs the *mean* of that, but not its *jitter*. If capture→detect ever varies frame-to-frame (load, contention), strum timing wobbles by that much. The clean fix is to have `video.c` stamp a capture timestamp into `Video_FrameInfo` and have CV use it instead of the task tick — then `strike_at` is anchored to when the photons actually arrived. Worth a decision: accept (probably sub-frame today) or fix.

**2. Multi-producer wire arbitration is cooperative, with no central arbiter.** `timing_pipeline`, `manual_control`, and `game_controller` all call `FretboardLink_Send`; hand-off is done by each calling `TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(false)` to quiet the pipeline before taking the wire. There's no single owner guaranteeing exactly one producer is live — it's convention. That's the practical, present-day face of open **Q11**. Fine while modes are manually exclusive, but a real thing to formalize (a small "who owns the wire" arbiter in the actuator sink) before adding more producers.

## Quick cleanups (I can do these now)

**3. Stale `TP_TICK_MS` comment.** The comment says *"5 ms keeps jitter well under our 16 ms detector cadence"* but the value is `2u` ([timing_pipeline.c:29-33](firmware/marvin/default/src/game/timing_pipeline.c#L29)). Doc/code mismatch — one-word fix.

**4. Dead variable `s_last_frame_us`.** Written once ([timing_pipeline.c:374](firmware/marvin/default/src/game/timing_pipeline.c#L374)), never read. Remove it.

## Minor / already tracked

- **`manual_control` still in `actuator/`** — the Q1 loose end (operator override, candidate for `ui/`). Low value to move on its own.
- **Actuator advance is a single scalar** (no per-bit / fret-vs-strum) — already noted in the journal for when a solenoid rig exists.

My take: **#3 and #4** are worth knocking out now (trivial, real). **#1** is the most interesting correctness item and worth a short decision. **#2** is Q11 — leave it tracked until another producer forces it.

Want me to fix #3/#4, and/or dig into #1?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-15 18:34:50Z)**_

Done — #1, #3, #4 fixed; #2 recorded as an open question for later.

**#1 — capture-time anchoring (the substantive one):** `Video_FrameInfo` now carries `timestamp_us`, stamped in the ISC frame-done IRQ (`on_frame_done`) via `xTaskGetTickCountFromISR()`. `cv_marvin_v1` copies `frame->timestamp_us` instead of resampling the tick at detect time, so capture→detect scheduling jitter no longer leaks into `strike_at_ms`. Removed the now-dead `CV_US_PER_TICK`, and set `timestamp_us = 0` in the synchronous `Video_GetFrameInfo` so the new field is never garbage for its callers (none use it).

**#3 — stale comment:** `TP_TICK_MS` block now says "2 ms" to match the `2u` value.

**#4 — dead variable:** removed `s_last_frame_us` (write-only).

**#2 — deferred:** recorded in Open questions as the present-day form of Q11 — three cooperative producers on the wire, hand-off via `TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(false)`, no central arbiter. Flagged the "who owns the wire" arbiter in `fretboard_link` as the eventual fix.

Files touched: `video/video.h`, `video/video.c`, `detector/cv_marvin_v1.c`, `game/timing_pipeline.c`, plus the journal. Only behavioral change is the reduced timing jitter from #1; the rest is inert. Nothing committed — say the word if you want these committed (I'd group them as one "capture-time anchoring + cleanups" commit).
